headline: Taking stock of his first bills
summary: In his Assembly diary Roosevelt reviews his early bills: a new aqueduct he doubts will pass, and a plan to elect aldermen by Assembly district that he expects to win despite fellow Republicans John Brodsky and Crane, whom he skewers. He also proposes a new public park for the city's 24th ward.

events.detail: Assembly diary entry on his bills and his Republican critics
Proposes a park for the 24th ward of New York City

tr_quotes.text: I have introduced several bills, the most important being one to build a new aqueduct which has no chance of passing. I also have one to make aldermen elected by assembly districts, which I expect to have pass in spite of the opposition of some of my New York Republican colleagues, such as Brodsky the German stalwart, a good natured little fellow but the lowest kind of spoils politician, and Crane, whose intellectual capacity about equals that of an average balloon.

references.title: Diary of the New York Legislature

uncertain: OCR 'inake' corrected to 'make'. Brodsky's first name John taken from the March 29 entry.

headline: Naming Gould and Sage on the floor
summary: Late in the day, with the 'Black Horse Cavalry' gone home, Roosevelt forces debate on the Westbrook resolution and wins a vote to take it up. tr_quotes.text: Mr. Spee-kar, . . . the men who were mainly concerned in this fraud are known throughout New York as men whose financial dishonesty is a matter of common notoriety. I make that statement deliberately; that the three or four wealthy stock gamblers who are interested in those read; are men who would be barely trusted in financial operations by any reputable businessman...
I am aware that it ought to have been done by a man of more experience, .. . but as nobody else chose to demand it, I certainly would in the interest... of New York.
